extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary 1942 newspaper coverage summarizing wartime government orders, regulations and policy decisions (rationing, price controls, transport and military allowances). Not a how-to or formal guideline document but reports statutory/administrative requirements and proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landlord registration under OPA rent-control
rubrics_metrics.description: Landlords in Federal rent-control areas must register all dwelling accommodations under new OPA regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a new OPA regulation; OPA regional offices are being enlarged to administer rules. (Context: part of the Office of Price Administration measures announced to implement rent-control.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal price ceiling / price-freeze policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The OPA has set up a universal price ceiling; Price Administrator Henderson froze the ceiling price at which manufacturers would sell virtually all types of consumer goods and the general freeze order 'takes March prices along the line ... and holds it fast until adjustment can be made as to what adjustments are needed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Merle Fainsod named to administer the Retail Trade and Services Division overseeing the universal price ceiling. The article records expected effects, criticisms from labor and business, and notes that interpretation and fair adjustments will be essential to make controls workable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline rationing allocation by need; supplemental cards
rubrics_metrics.description: When gasoline rationing starts, motorists will be given gas according to their needs; persons necessarily using greater mileage may apply for supplemental cards. 'Cards B1, B2 and B3 will be issued to passenger car owners who state in an application that their gas needs fall within certain specified mileage limits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications require mileage from home to work/commuting point and statements about efforts to reduce mileage. Doctors, war workers and others whose vocations require greater mileage may apply. Any registrant who feels special hardship may later appeal to the local rationing board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on abandonment of oil and gas wells
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petroleum Coordination Office directed that no oil or gas well be abandoned until the well is incapable of producing enough oil or gas 'to pay costs of labor, maintenance and taxes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale given: 'It is essential ... that the maximum recovery of known reserves of petroleum in the United States be obtained.' Notice of intent to abandon should be filed with the director of production at least 30 days before abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal directive to taxicab owners to conserve service
rubrics_metrics.description: Government ordered taxicab owners to quit performing 'non-essential services' for Mr. and Mrs. America, stop 'cruising,' encourage multiple riding and other measures to obtain the maximum efficiency from each cab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issued as part of wider transportation conservation measures due to rubber and gasoline shortages; intended to increase efficiency of available taxi resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal employees asked to reduce number of commuting automobiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal employees were told to 'substantially' reduce the number of automobiles necessary to take them to and from work, according to guidance reported to reduce private transportation of factory and office workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a broader program aimed at immediate transport curtailment due to rubber and gasoline shortages; the President sent letters urging state and local governments to adopt similar measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ration-card application information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In applying for a ration (gas) card each motorist will give the mileage from his home to his place of work or commuting point, the nature of his work, the shortest mileage capable of performing his work and the average daily mileage customarily driven in such work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants will be asked whether they 'are making every reasonable effort to reduce this mileage by using public transportation and by doubling up with your neighbors?'; supplemental cards issued if need is demonstrated; appeals permitted to local boards for special hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed military dependents allowance schedule (legislative proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure (pending in the House) would raise minimum pay and provide scheduled allowances for dependents: wives and children (Class A) would receive $20 monthly taken from the pay of enlisted men with graduated government additions (e.g., $20 for wife with no child, $30 for wife and one child, $10 for each additional child); Class B (parents, grandchildren, brothers/sisters) allowances optional with limits (top $50 monthly) and various specified amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as the structure of a proposed bill under Senate consideration; debate recorded over flexible authority for Federal Security Agency to supplement payments in 'hardship cases' and objections that the proposal had no top/bottom limit for such supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisitioning of storage materials and warehouses for Allied support
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic Warfare reported requisitioning 2,700,000 burlap and jute bags in United States warehouses for the French government to be sent to Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic for sugar; restrictions on shipments of coffee to the United States for storage were removed to aid American hemisphere countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative wartime measures intended to assist allied and American-hemisphere food/shipping needs; reported as executive actions by agencies to adapt to shipping shortages.
